# Punt BLK: Player Targets

**Summary.** Punt BLK suits our 9-cat league because blocks swing a lot from year to year and you will still win the category some weeks without trying. The risk is that blocks move with rebounds and FG%. If you only draft low-block players, you can lose REB and FG% too. Use Brunson at 20 to 25 USD and cheap guards like Pritchard and Quickley for threes and assists. Then protect FG% with efficient pieces like Tre Jones and Gordon, and keep real rebounding bigs on the roster.

## Why blocks are a good punt

Blocks are very variable from year to year. That makes them a good category to punt. High-variance categories like steals, blocks, threes and FT% still fall your way some weeks by surprise. Stable, high-volume categories like points and assists are bad to punt. In our weekly H2H format, giving up blocks costs less than giving up points or assists. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1785), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2722))

In practice, plan to win the other eight categories most weeks. Do not spend auction dollars on blocks. Count any blocks you get from your center and forwards as a bonus. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2722))

## The trap: blocks travel with REB and FG%

High blocks go with high rebounds and high FG%. If you chase only low-block players, your rebounds and FG% will suffer too. Then a one-category punt quietly becomes a three-category punt, and three lost categories every week is too many to win in 9-cat H2H. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=588), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=620))

So the rule for our draft is simple. Punt blocks by not paying for them. Do not punt them by avoiding every player who blocks shots. Keep at least your C slot and one Util slot for players who bring rebounds and good FG%, even if they also block shots. None of the six player notes below lists rebounds as a strength, so this target list cannot cover REB on its own. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=620), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=588))

The notes pull in two directions here. One view says blocks are among the best categories to punt because they are high variance. Another view warns that the big man side is tightly linked. Only rebounds, blocks and FG% move together, which makes a big man build harder to execute. Read together, punting blocks is sound, but it needs care in the frontcourt. It is not a free pass to load up on guards and wings. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2722), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=819), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=620))

## Guard targets: points, threes, assists, FT%

Jalen Brunson is the anchor guard for this build, but only at the right price. Category experts see him as a fourth-round player, not a top-30 one. Let others pay 30 USD or more. Bid up to about 20 to 25 USD for his points, FT%, threes and assists. He blocks almost nothing, so he fits the punt cleanly. ([Jalen Brunson](../profiles/players/jalen-brunson.md))

Payton Pritchard and Immanuel Quickley are the cheap guard layer. Pritchard brings threes, solid FT%, assists and low turnovers. Cap him at about 5 USD. Quickley helps in threes and assists and is a value pick in single digits. His 43.5% FG% is a small drag, so do not pair him with other weak FG% shooters. ([Payton Pritchard](../profiles/players/payton-pritchard.md), [Immanuel Quickley](../profiles/players/immanuel-quickley.md))

Remember that high assists go with high turnovers. If you stack Brunson and Quickley for assists, balance them with low-turnover players like Pritchard or Tre Jones so TO does not slip. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=588), [Payton Pritchard](../profiles/players/payton-pritchard.md), [Tre Jones](../profiles/players/tre-jones.md))

## Cheap pieces that protect FG%

Tre Jones is projected for a 54.5% FG% from a guard, with assists and few turnovers. That is exactly the kind of player who keeps FG% alive in a punt BLK build. He is a 1 USD last pick at most and more likely a waiver add. Add him if his minutes stay around 23 to 25, or if Powell or Giddey miss time or Powell is traded. ([Tre Jones](../profiles/players/tre-jones.md), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=620))

Aaron Gordon is a decent FG% forward with some threes and assists, and he is eligible at F and C. He played only 36 and 51 games in the last two seasons, and experts see no upside. Let others draft him. If he goes undrafted, check his minutes and his hamstring and calf health early. Use him as a streamer, since Denver has few back-to-backs. ([Aaron Gordon](../profiles/players/aaron-gordon.md))

Saddiq Bey brings FT%, threes and few turnovers, but his FG% is below average. He is the kind of low-block player who drags FG% down with blocks. He sits near our 144-player cut. Leave him on waivers unless Mosley starts him or closes games with him. ([Saddiq Bey](../profiles/players/saddiq-bey.md), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=620))

## Draft day and early season checklist

On 2026-10-18, set price caps before the draft: Brunson about 20 to 25 USD, Pritchard about 5 USD, Quickley single digits, and Tre Jones 1 USD at most. Do not pay for Gordon or Bey. After each guard you win, check your running FG% picture. If you already have Quickley, the next cheap pick should help FG%, not hurt it. ([Jalen Brunson](../profiles/players/jalen-brunson.md), [Payton Pritchard](../profiles/players/payton-pritchard.md), [Immanuel Quickley](../profiles/players/immanuel-quickley.md), [Tre Jones](../profiles/players/tre-jones.md), [Aaron Gordon](../profiles/players/aaron-gordon.md), [Saddiq Bey](../profiles/players/saddiq-bey.md))

In the first weeks, watch Brunson's minutes, back-to-back rest and wrist. The Knicks plan to be careful with starters for the first 30 or so games. Watch whether Pritchard starts and gets about 30 minutes, whether Quickley's three-point volume rises next to Kawhi, and the Jones, Gordon and Bey triggers above. Use FAB on whichever trigger hits first, within our 6 adds per week. ([Jalen Brunson](../profiles/players/jalen-brunson.md), [Payton Pritchard](../profiles/players/payton-pritchard.md), [Immanuel Quickley](../profiles/players/immanuel-quickley.md), [Tre Jones](../profiles/players/tre-jones.md), [Aaron Gordon](../profiles/players/aaron-gordon.md), [Saddiq Bey](../profiles/players/saddiq-bey.md))
